survey: A fruit plate on a wooden table. A clear, shallow round glass plate rests flat on the tabletop, and its elliptical rim looks the same all the way around. A tall watermelon wedge stands upright at the back. It leans on its cut side, with the red flesh and seeds facing the camera and the green rind along the curved right edge. Its base is hidden behind the other fruit, but it sits inside the plate's footprint. At the left is a green grape bunch. A woody stem with one leaf goes into the top of the bunch, and the grapes rest on the plate. Two strawberries sit in the middle with their leafy tops still on. One rests on the plate in front; the other sits behind it, against the watermelon. Four blueberries with crowns sit on the plate at the front right. Two orange wedges sit at the right, peel side down, with their segments facing up toward the camera. The front wedge rests on the plate, and the back wedge leans on the front wedge and the watermelon. Each piece of fruit touches either the plate or a fruit that supports it. None float, pass through each other or carry made-up parts. The counts are believable, and the simplifications (grapes with no single stems, rounded orange segments) are normal for stylized card art.
